content: The tesla, denoted by the symbol T, is the SI-derived unit used to measure the magnetic field, specifically magnetic flux density. One tesla is defined as one weber per square meter. This unit was officially established in 1960 and named in honor of Nikola Tesla, a renowned inventor, scientist, and electrical engineer. In terms of conversions, one tesla is equivalent to 10,000 gauss (G), a unit commonly used in the CGS (centimeter-gram-second) system. Therefore, 10 gauss is equal to 1 millitesla (mT). Additionally, one tesla is equal to 1,000,000,000 (10⁹) gammas (γ), a unit frequently used in geophysics.
